meta.author: Demo home
meta.summary: Two releases to catch up on: update the Z-Wave JS app first, expect some dashboard names to change, and the rest is new features for the lights, buttons, and cameras this home already has.

items.title: Turn off Tuya fans when the speed is set to 0%

assessment.summary: Setting a Tuya fan's speed to 0% now turns it off.
assessment.impact: The Bathroom extractor fan turns off when its speed slider goes to 0%, instead of staying on at the lowest speed.

assessment.summary: Home Assistant Cloud is being renamed Home Assistant Link in December, and remote access got faster with more servers and automatic server picking.
Maps now draw OpenStreetMap vector tiles on your device, fetched through Home Assistant, with redesigned markers and a dark style.
The user profile is split into short sections (appearance, localization, this browser, security), and people can now change their own name and picture.

items.title: The best automation feature you never used

assessment.summary: Trigger IDs get a proper editor: in a Triggered by condition you tick the triggers to match, and Home Assistant manages the IDs.
assessment.impact: Most rooms here have two or three motion-light automations, such as Garden motion lights 1 to 3. Each set could become one automation with a Triggered by condition.

assessment.summary: Matter adds switches for leak sensor alarms and for one-touch locking, plus frequency and power factor for power meters.
assessment.impact: The Hallway door lock is a Matter lock, so you can now decide whether one touch on its keypad locks the door.

assessment.summary: Tuya supports more devices: DIN rail meters, breakers, EV chargers, water valves, and more readings for three-phase meters.
ESPHome devices can open the connection to Home Assistant themselves, for networks where Home Assistant can't reach them.
Reolink can pan and tilt the lenses of multi-lens cameras behind an NVR or Home Hub.
Roborock wet and dry vacuums now update in real time.
Z-Wave gets automation editor conditions and triggers for node status, configuration parameters, and other values.
UniFi Protect supports the key fob and relay inputs, and API-key-only mode covers more devices and settings.
Binary sensors get a glass break device class, treated as a security sensor.
The Z-Wave network map can show the real mesh between devices.
Climate fan modes can be set by voice.
The legacy mode of the login provider is removed, and usernames are always lowercase without surrounding spaces.
assessment.impact: Only matters if Home Assistant showed a repair about usernames.

assessment.summary: The mqtt.publish and mqtt.dump actions now require an administrator when a person calls them.
assessment.impact: No automation or script here calls mqtt.publish.

assessment.summary: State conditions that combine for with an attribute, a list of states, or another entity's state now fail validation.
assessment.impact: No automation here has a state condition.

assessment.summary: HACS becomes the built-in Marketplace under Settings, for installing community integrations, cards, themes, and templates without a restart.
Targets can now leave out entities, devices, areas, floors, or labels, and the exclusion keeps applying as things are added.
assessment.impact: The sunset automations close every blind in an area; an exclusion could keep one open, such as the Office blinds on work days, without listing the others by hand.

assessment.summary: Dashboard sections can be copied or cut and pasted, also into another view or dashboard.
Automatic dashboard sections pick their own cards, such as every light on a floor or every entity of one device, and stay current as devices change.
New Date card and Alert badge, a color option for the Sensor card, buttons or a slider for target temperatures, and a visual editor for the Alert card.
Light tiles get a hue strip with an optional saturation slider.

items.title: Name it once, Home Assistant adds the context

assessment.summary: Entities are named once and Home Assistant adds the device or area around them where it helps, so renaming a device renames its entities.
assessment.impact: See Entity names under You'll notice for what changes on the dashboards.

items.title: Forms that ask only what they need

assessment.summary: Setup forms and blueprints show a field only when an earlier answer makes it relevant.

items.title: From power to energy in one step

assessment.summary: The Energy dashboard offers to derive an energy sensor from a power-only sensor, and the same for gas and water flow.
The Activity panel filters by what triggered a change, traces link to the script run they started, and integrations with debug logging show their own live log.
Matter 1.5 cameras are supported, and a Labs preview adds two-way audio to camera streams.
assessment.impact: The Reolink doorbells in the Hallway and Garden can use two-way audio once it is turned on in Labs, as long as they stream over RTSP and the app is opened over HTTPS.

items.title: Store backups and media on local drives

assessment.summary: Internal and USB drives can hold backups, media, and shared files, and restores no longer copy the whole backup first.

items.title: Reach the far corners with LoRaWAN

assessment.summary: Home Assistant connects to LoRaWAN network servers such as ChirpStack and The Things Network, with a new LoRaWAN page under Connectivity.

items.title: Batteryless switches with Zigbee Green Power

assessment.summary: ZHA now pairs Zigbee Green Power devices, such as batteryless wall switches that run on the press itself.
assessment.impact: This home runs ZHA, so a batteryless switch (a Friends of Hue switch, for example) could join the Zigbee network and drive the motion-light rooms by hand.

assessment.summary: ESPHome devices can share a serial port over the network, which ZHA can use for a Zigbee adapter plugged into one.
Shelly adds support for the BLU TRV, a Last seen sensor for battery devices, and a combined cover position and tilt action.
Tuya supports heated towel racks, irrigation valves, and the missing switches on multi-gang wall switches.
UniFi Protect supports the Alarm Hub, and API-key-only mode gains chimes, doorbell messages, and pan and tilt.
Each ZHA group gets its own device, which can have its own area.
MQTT devices can have child devices, and the MQTT entity editor gets a unit picker.
WLED adds an AudioReactive switch, a next-playlist-entry button, and temperature and humidity sensors for devices with those usermods.
The Group integration can combine several calendars into one.
The Alert card only colors and pulses during an alert, and its color option is now alert_color.
assessment.impact: Only YAML dashboards that added the card by hand need the new option name.

assessment.summary: The new sun and calendar event triggers now read the sign of their offset: negative fires before the event, positive after.
assessment.impact: The sunset automations use the classic sun trigger with a negative offset, which this does not change.

assessment.summary: Device trackers from network scanners such as UniFi, FRITZ!Box, and Nmap now always have a device, and new ones start disabled.
assessment.impact: Alex's and Sam's trackers come from the companion app, not a network scanner.

assessment.summary: Entity names are now built from the entity name plus its device name.
assessment.impact: Dashboard cards without their own name will show names like Hallway motion sensor Occupancy. The old name stays as a voice alias, and automations are not affected. Set a name on a card, or rename the device, where you want it shorter.

assessment.summary: Matter concentration sensors use the device's own unit, climate entities resume their last mode when turned on, and tilt-only covers become tilt covers.
assessment.impact: The Matter devices here are bulbs, up-and-down blinds, and a lock, none of which change.

assessment.summary: MQTT entities without a unique_id no longer create a device from their device settings.
assessment.impact: The Zigbee2MQTT devices here are discovered with unique IDs.

assessment.summary: Home Assistant no longer installs Python packages into the deps folder of the config directory.
assessment.impact: Only Home Assistant Core outside a virtual environment is affected.

assessment.summary: Multi-channel Tuya devices put each channel's entities on a child device, so their names change.
assessment.impact: The only Tuya device here is the Bathroom extractor fan, which has one channel and keeps its name.

assessment.summary: The deprecated HDR mode switch and the read-only UP Sense setting entities are removed.
assessment.impact: No automation or script here uses them; a repair would list any that did.

assessment.summary: The S400 scale's impedance sensors are corrected and split into low and high.
assessment.impact: The Xiaomi devices here are climate sensors, not scales.

assessment.summary: Z-Wave now needs zwave-js-server 3.11.0 or later, and multi-endpoint devices get a child device per endpoint.
assessment.impact: The radiator valves, thermostat, and door and window sensors all run on Z-Wave, and the too-warm and door automations depend on them. Entity IDs stay the same, so the automations keep working once the server is current.
assessment.action: Update the Z-Wave JS app to 1.9.0 or later before upgrading Home Assistant.

assessment.summary: ZHA groups with group entities move from the coordinator to their own device.
assessment.impact: This home has no ZHA groups, and no automation targets the coordinator.

verdict.reason: Update the Z-Wave JS app to 1.9.0 or later before you upgrade, or the radiator valves and door sensors go offline. Nothing else in this home needs a change.
